source_note: All three arms produced by the real _build_game_level on the PRODUCTION source (data_delivery/pbp_defense_20260925.parquet, the 27-column projection of pitches.parquet). The participants and widen_noil arms are carried over unchanged from lineup_il_ab_20260926_prod.json -- neither registers il_stints, so rebuilding the table cannot move them. Only the il arm was rebuilt.
fix: il_stints.parquet is now reconciled against observed plate appearances (build_il_stints.reconcile_with_plate_appearances): a stint ends at the batter's first plate appearance after the placement, so no interval can span a game he was in the lineup for. Residual defect (player-games the table calls on-IL while the batter batted) 3,522 -> 0; 19 same-date placement/appearance pairs remain by design and are not counted. Regex and time-cap alternatives were measured first and are strictly worse (recall/contract-selection closes recover 29% of the defect, a 120-day cap 68%); unlike a cap this rule never releases a date the batter did not play, so it costs zero genuine absences. The build now refuses to write a table whose residual exceeds _MAX_RESIDUAL_ON_IL_PGAMES.
verdict: The defect is fixed and the feature stays, but it is honestly neutral: removing the pathology did NOT make the IL filter a win. il_swap vs baseline is flat on logloss (+0.0002, t=+0.26) with d_auc +0.0021, and the IL flag on top of the widened pool is still a small net negative (d_logloss +0.0011, t=+1.45; d_auc -0.0038). What the filter DOES buy is calibration: the widened pool alone drifts +0.0056 ECE and FAILS RFE_ECE_GUARD, while widened+filter drifts +0.0040 and passes both guards. So the shipped combination is defensible as a calibration control, not as an accuracy gain. Widening alone remains the only arm with a real signal (d_auc +0.0059, d_logloss -0.0009).
supersedes: lineup_il_ab_20260926.json (contaminated source), lineup_il_ab_20260926_prod.json (correct source, unreconciled table)
